title: Ibn Battuta: Mali and the Sahara, 1351–54
summary: With the salt caravan from Sijilmasa across the Sahara to Walata and the court of Mansa Sulayman, down the Niger by Timbuktu to Gao, and home by Takedda, the Hoggar and Tuat in winter snow.

events.label: Taghaza, the salt town
events.text: Twenty-five days out of Sijilmasa, a village where the houses and the mosque are built of blocks of salt and roofed with camel skins, worked by slaves of the Massufa. He spent ten hard days there, the water brackish.

events.label: Walata
events.text: Among the Massufa of Walata no man takes his name from his father but from his mother's brother, and sons do not inherit, only sisters' sons. The women, he says, were more highly regarded than the men, and the men without jealousy, though strict in their prayers.

events.label: Two months ill
events.text: Ten days after he reached the capital, all six of his party fell ill from a dish of qafi, something like taro; one died. He fainted at the dawn prayer and was ill for two months.

events.label: Timbuktu
events.text: Most of the town were Massufa, under a governor called Farba Musa. He saw the grave of Abu Ishaq al-Sahili, the Granadan poet who came back to Mali with Mansa Musa from his pilgrimage and built for him.

events.label: Takedda: copper, and the call home
events.text: A town of red stone, its water tainted by the copper mines, where slaves smelted copper into rods used as money. Here the sultan of Morocco's order to come home reached him. He left with a big caravan carrying some six hundred enslaved women.
